revisions.why: Drone-2525 1st Pass persisted verbatim; the CRS ladder opens at Version 00.00.

The MoT ladder replaces the four-tier fidelity table: 5 compute bands x 5 resolution steps, 1.1 the arcade rung and the fastest. Demand and capability are separated. Multi-sensor fusion EO->CHEM sheds from the top and never sheds EO. The unit holds 1080p30 and names every step down. A self-test walks the ladder in 6 to 15 minutes and reports the rung this machine actually holds.

The flying modes. A fixed-wing VTOL hovers on rotors and cruises on a wing, with the stall speed as the number the transition turns on. A machine may hold the pilot's seat, the camera operator's seat, or both — and a machine that is aiming must ask a named person before any shot, a gate with no bypass. All four of the operator's modes are unlocked.

Shared Intent, as a placeholder: a key group switched on or off, invited by a code and a scannable square, answering a real-time call on the decision the round already has. The group advises and a named person still decides. Recognition uses the three fixed heart values the pod ladder already declares, rather than a fourth invented for this feature.

Two people on two devices: one flies, one works the camera, and neither can do the other's job. Optimised against a measurement on a processor slowed ten times rather than against a desktop that hides every change. Nine runs of every gate with zero drift, ten spiral checks, SSSES 93.

Forty-two aircraft, 21 against 21, inside the ladder's budget at every rung. A five-level authority ladder on the band that already exists, with the invariant unbent on every rung. And an SSSES scorer rewritten to measure rather than assert, which dropped the score before the work lifted it to 96.

The fixed-wing is declared at the 1.111 m foil, proportional, from the early Security-2525 drawing — and the drawing's axes are declared with it, because the shipped extent had span, depth and nose-to-tail under each other's names and every consumer inherited the permutation.

The wing is derived from the drawing instead of asserted beside it. wingAreaM2 was 0.9 m2 against a real planform of 0.3092 m2, so the round had been flying a wing three times the size of the one on screen. Stall moves 8.43 -> 14.38 m/s, and the quad's acceleration is now derived from the stall rather than typed, so the transition stays reachable on any airframe.
The aircraft is the FOIL on this surface and nowhere says its other name, with one declared exception for the provenance path. The game answers at /drone-2525 as well as /main/Drone-2525.

Lasers, shields and time on target. A fluence model rather than hit points, so range is the thing that matters: 0.79 s to disable at 100 m, 5.15 s at 400 m, 13.67 s at 700 m. A defeated aircraft is disabled and flown down under control at 1.6 m/s; there is no state called destroyed.

Ten CRS rows for the overnight work: the beam and shield rules, the safe descent, the lighting inside the vector law, the two sizes and the square-cube law between them, the N ladder and what it measured about the person, the winners' circle and its one-ninth cut, the floor that must be cleared by name, the FOIL naming rule, and the address the game answers at.

geometry.sourceNote: The drawing's OWN header is the authority: xbat_3rdpass_wireframe.obj:2 reads '# X span, Y depth, Z vertical nose-up axis', and xbat_3rdpass_wireframe.py:13-15 repeats it. The carried model declared forward:'x', which was wrong, and scripts/build-airframe-glyph.mjs believed it — so the shipped extent was three correct measurements under three wrong names. Corrected 2026-09-16; see docs/asks/2026-09-16_foil_1m_five_levels_world.md.

bodyAxes.note: How the drawing's axes map into the app's body frame (forward +x, right +y, up +z). The model is drawn nose-UP, standing on its tail, so its vertical axis is the fuselage.

geometry.scaleNote: Operator 2026-09-16: 'make fix wing aircraft 1 m foil and proportional'. 1.111 x 0.7777 is the demo scale of his own FOIL package and is proportional to the full 11.111 x 7.777 to within 0.07 mm on the span. Against the SOURCE drawing it is a 3.07% stretch along the fuselage, which is intentional: his manifest specifies non-uniform scaling and gives the rule for depth, quoted next.
geometry.depthRule: depth scaled with geometric mean of span and length scales (FOIL_full_11_111x7_777_manifest.json, dimensions_m.depth_scale_note)
geometry.planformMethod: Integrated from the drawing itself: group the 901 vertices by nose-to-tail station (the loft has 94 distinct ribs), take the half-span at each, trapezoid the full width between them, then scale by span x length. Bucketing into fixed bins does NOT converge — the ribs are discrete, so empty bins read as zero area and the answer halves every time you double the bins. 361.6614 m2 at the source, 0.3092 m2 at the foil, which is 72% of a plain delta of the same span and length.
geometry.namingRule: Drone-2525 calls this aircraft the FOIL and does not use its other name (operator 2026-09-16: 'which we will not say in Drone-2525 so as not to upset Shield AI'). The `source` and `sourceNote` fields above are the ONLY place the other name may appear anywhere on this surface, and only as a filesystem path and a correction record — a derivation that cannot name its source cannot be verified. Enforced by frontend/tests/drone-naming.test.mjs, which refuses the token everywhere else.

airframe.note: Brochure-class public figures for a 5 kg VTOL, EXCEPT wingAreaM2, which is no longer asserted: it is derived from the drawing by geometry.planformMethod and gated by frontend/tests/airframe-truth.test.mjs. It read 0.9 m2 until 2026-09-16 — 2.9x the area the aircraft actually has — because the physics record and the drawing were two unconnected descriptions of 'the aircraft' that never met in code. BOUNDING ESTIMATE ONLY - not design evidence.

battery.note: Reserve is never spent by the sim; endurance is quoted on the usable 80%.

beam.note: BOUNDING ESTIMATE ONLY - not design evidence and not a real weapon. Chosen so the dwell a player feels lands where the game wants it: well under a second in close, a few seconds at the gimbal's declared range, and a slog beyond it. Range matters because the beam spreads and the air absorbs, which is the one physical fact the whole engagement turns on. Fine-track lock is 0.35 s: the director needs that long back on a target before full power, so flicking between targets is a losing tactic and holding is the game.

defences.note: Independence Day: the shield absorbs first and nothing reaches the airframe until it fails. Ender's Game and the operator's own words: a defeated aircraft is DISABLED and flown down under control, never deleted in the air. Battle House: it comes back, it is not exterminated.

sensor.note: Edge extraction budget comes out of the frame before the renderer (lib/wire-core/fidelity.ts).

targets.note: Every building door is a pop-up target. Tag it by CAPTURE (store the sensor edge set) then SHOOT (line of sight must reach it). The up-window is not a taste value: a target must stay up longer than the worst swing to reach it (4s at 45°/s for half a turn) plus time to aim and press, or the round is unwinnable by construction. Gated in tests/drone-gimbal.test.mjs.

crs.title: The MoT ladder: five compute bands by five resolution steps
crs.statement: Detail and sensing are asked for on a 25-rung ladder, 1.1 through 5.5, where the band is the edge-compute class and the step is the resolution; rung 1.1 is the 1983 vector arcade and is the fastest picture the machine can make.
crs.metric: ladder monotonic in both axes; 1.1 asks for more frames than 5.5
crs.dtm: 25 rungs selectable
crs.stretch: a robot picks its own rung unattended

crs.title: Demand and capability are separate, and never mixed
crs.statement: What the picture asks for (the rung) and what the machine can deliver (the HAL class and the measured frame rate) are different quantities held in different modules, and only calibration is allowed to reconcile them.
crs.metric: a richer rung never asks for a faster picture
crs.dtm: the old inverted four-tier table is gone
crs.stretch: the same split serves every 2525 domain

crs.title: Multi-sensor fusion, shed from the top and never blind
crs.statement: Sensing runs EO, IR, ACOUSTIC, MAG and CHEM, one more module per compute band; when the frame will not hold, modules are shed from the top of that ladder and EO is never shed, because a unit that cannot see is not degraded but blind.
crs.metric: EO survives every degradation path
crs.dtm: five modules declared per band
crs.stretch: a real sensor replaces the simulated one behind the same interface

crs.title: Hold 1080p30, and name every step down from it
crs.statement: The unit tries to hold a 1920x1080 30 Hz reference stream; when it cannot it sheds a sensor module, then resolution, then frame rate, in that order, and every step is named on screen rather than taken silently.
crs.metric: degradation order fixed; climb needs sustained headroom
crs.dtm: stream ladder live in the HUD
crs.stretch: the same ladder drives a real encoder

crs.title: Self-test: the rung this machine actually holds, in 6 to 15 minutes
crs.statement: Pointed at a new board or a new sensor, the unit walks the ladder from 1.1 upward under real drawing load, measures a sustained frame rate at each rung, and reports the highest rung it holds at the reference stream, inside a declared 6 to 15 minute budget.
crs.metric: dwell derived from the budget; sweep stops early after two failures
crs.dtm: a saved result file naming the ceiling
crs.stretch: run headless on the robot itself

crs.title: The robot may pick its own compute class
crs.statement: Three compute classes are declared with their frame budgets and sensor costs, and AUTO lets the unit choose its own class from the frame rate it measures rather than from a label someone typed.
crs.metric: AUTO thresholds derived from the budgets themselves
crs.dtm: PI / EDGE-SOC / ACCELERATOR selectable
crs.stretch: a fourth class added without touching a caller

crs.title: Shared Intent: a key group, switched on or off
crs.statement: A closed group of named people may be switched on to weigh in on decisions; off is the normal state and the round behaves exactly as it does without them.
crs.metric: no call can open while it is off; switching off closes any open call
crs.dtm: the switch and a closed roster
crs.stretch: the group is a real polling session on Cube 1

crs.title: Key members only, by invitation
crs.statement: Reaching the group's call needs a code issued to named people; an empty roster produces no invitation rather than an open link, and the right code in the wrong hands is refused.
crs.metric: both halves must hold: on the roster, and a live code
crs.dtm: a code and a scannable square
crs.stretch: delivery through the operator's own channel

crs.title: The group advises; a named person decides
crs.statement: Consensus is shown beside the decision a person is about to make and can never make it: no function in the consensus engine can retire a shot request or open the authority gate, and a unanimous group changes nothing about what may fire.
crs.metric: the two modules do not import each other; unanimity does not open the gate
crs.dtm: advice beside the question
crs.stretch: the same rule wherever a crowd meets an authority

crs.title: Volunteer input, recognised on the ladder that already exists
crs.statement: Answering is voluntary and silence counts as nothing; a contribution is recognised as noted, and as adopted only after the decision went the way it argued, using the three fixed heart values the pod ladder already declares rather than a fourth invented here.
crs.metric: no value outside the declared ladder; silence earns nothing
crs.dtm: a readable record of what was valued
crs.stretch: entries reach the Cube 8 append-only ledger

crs.title: A seat may only send what that seat controls
crs.statement: The pilot flies and cannot aim, photograph or shoot; the targeteer aims, photographs and shoots and cannot fly; a message whose payload does not belong to the seat that sent it is refused on the way in as well as on the way out.

crs.stretch: the same rule for a third seat

crs.statement: Performance is reported from real painted frames on a processor slowed ten times, because a desktop pins every case at the refresh rate and hides any change; the heaviest case is the one quoted.

crs.title: Nine runs, or it is not determinism
crs.statement: Every gate runs nine times and every reproducible artefact — the model hash, the schedule, a flown path, a crew code, the rung verdicts — must be byte-identical across all nine, and the spiral is asserted in both directions rather than asserted about.
crs.metric: 1,395 checks per run, nine runs, zero drift, ten spiral checks

crs.stretch: the same harness for every domain

crs.title: Forty-two aircraft, twenty-one against twenty-one
crs.statement: An engagement puts 42 aircraft in the air as two opposing sides of 21, held in flat columns so a tick allocates nothing, and drawn as an overlay in the arena's own camera batched into a handful of paths.

crs.title: One budget, two consumers: the aircraft are the world
crs.statement: In an engagement the swarm takes its share of the rung's segment budget first and the Capitol block takes what is left, so at a poor rung the world thins rather than the aircraft vanishing; and every aircraft is drawn at the smallest size before any is given detail.
crs.metric: all 42 drawn at every one of the 25 rungs
crs.dtm: 42 drawn at rung 1.1 with the world at 112 segments
crs.stretch: the same rule wherever a budget is shared

crs.title: Five authority levels, and silence is never consent on any of them
crs.statement: Autonomy rides on the band that already exists: level 1 a named person per shot, level 5 the key group's live lean as a standing mandate it can end at once; at every level a named human decision exists before any machine shot, and what scales is the breadth of one decision rather than whether one happened.
crs.metric: a refusal from all five levels when nothing has been decided
crs.dtm: five levels selectable
crs.stretch: the ladder serves any domain with a machine and an authority

crs.title: A score that can fall
crs.statement: Every SSSES pillar is computed from evidence produced in the same run — authority checks, nine-run drift, measured frames against the declared reference, whether the projection memo demonstrably holds, and duplication and dead exports counted from the source — and a performance file measured at a different commit is refused rather than trusted.
crs.metric: no pillar is a literal; the score fell before it rose
crs.dtm: a score a reviewer can re-derive
crs.stretch: the same scorer for every domain

crs.title: The beam, the shield, and the time it takes
crs.statement: Engagement is a fluence model, not hit points: irradiance at the target falls with beam spread and atmospheric loss, so the same emitter needs under a second in close and seconds at reach, and a fine-track lock means a broken beam loses its progress. The shield absorbs first and nothing reaches the airframe until it fails.
crs.metric: the published dwell table is what the model computes, at every range
crs.dtm: a player learns to close and to hold, without being told
crs.stretch: a real emitter profile behind the same interface

crs.title: Nothing is destroyed in the air
crs.statement: A defeated aircraft is DISABLED and flown down under control to a safe landing. There is no reachable state called destroyed, and a beam on an aircraft already coming down changes nothing about its descent.
crs.metric: every state a beam can reach is one of five, and none of them is destroyed
crs.dtm: real machines over a real floor with people underneath
crs.stretch: a physical descent check before every match

crs.title: Lighting inside the vector law
crs.statement: The engagement reads from stroke colour and weight alone — tracking, absorbing, the moment the shield fails, burning, coming down — plus a shield ring drawn as a declared n-gon that shrinks as the shield is spent. No glow, no gradient, no bloom.
crs.metric: every stage names a palette role and a declared stroke weight
crs.dtm: forty-two engagements readable as shapes
crs.stretch: the same language on every 2525 surface

crs.title: One aircraft, two sizes
crs.statement: The mini foil scales to the full one by geometric similarity, with every derived quantity following the exponent it actually has: area as the square, mass as the cube, stall as the square root. The geometry, the proportions and every rule about materials or people are unchanged by the switch.
crs.metric: stall at the full size is the square root of the length ratio times the mini's, recomputed rather than asserted
crs.dtm: a demo at the Capitol at the size it will really be
crs.stretch: a third size needing one line and no arithmetic

crs.title: The same game at every N
crs.statement: The engagement runs at 1v1, 2v2 and every rung to 21v21 — 42 aircraft, 84 seats — from one model, so what breaks can be found on the way up rather than only at full strength. Each rung is measured for beam waste, contention, decision load and seats.
crs.metric: twenty-one rungs, three seeds each, twelve computed review lenses, all passing
crs.dtm: a complexity found at the rung where it appears
crs.stretch: the ladder run against a live crew

crs.title: The person is the bottleneck, and it is measured
crs.statement: The invariant that a machine shot needs a named human decision does not bend with N, so the decision load is measured at every rung and compared against what the people present can physically answer. Levels one to three put the decision with one person; four and five put it with a quorum of the key group, which is the only thing that raises a throughput ceiling.
crs.metric: no rung at the top authority level asks for more decisions than its approvers can answer
crs.dtm: an argument for the authority ladder from measurement, not assertion
crs.stretch: the same measurement against real approvers

crs.title: From open play to a real floor
crs.statement: Progression runs open play to the winners' circle to a tournament to a physical match. The cut is one ninth, the R-CORE recursion gate, floored and published with its cut line. The score is dominated by accuracy and by whether decisions were answered rather than by kills.
crs.metric: one ninth holds at every field size from nine to three hundred and ninety-nine
crs.dtm: the eleven per cent who want the real thing find it
crs.stretch: a season run end to end

crs.title: The last gate is not about skill
crs.statement: A physical match requires a NAMED safety officer, both crews present, the arena clear of anyone not in the match, and every machine's descent checked. None of those is a score, a perfect record opens none of them, and a refusal names the condition that is missing without discarding the entry.
crs.metric: a champion with a perfect record still cannot clear an arena
crs.dtm: nobody is hurt by a tournament
crs.stretch: a signed floor clearance on the record

crs.title: The aircraft is the FOIL
crs.statement: This surface calls the aircraft the FOIL and uses no other name for it — not in a label, a lexicon value, a CRS row, a component, a shipped document or an export. The geometry provenance path is the single declared exception, because a derivation that cannot name its source cannot be verified.
crs.metric: forty-four files scanned, the token refused outside two declared provenance fields
crs.dtm: a name we chose, used everywhere
crs.stretch: the provenance carried under a neutral path

crs.title: The address the game answers at
crs.statement: The game is served at /drone-2525 as well as at /main/Drone-2525. Both routes render the one component, their code is identical, and both are emitted to the static export — a route that compiles but does not emit is a 404 in production and green in CI.
crs.metric: both pages exist, import the same component, and appear in out/
crs.dtm: a link that works when it is handed to somebody
crs.stretch: the live site checked from outside the sandbox

crs.title: One seat geometry for every vehicle
crs.statement: The pilot's eye is at +0.18 L forward and +0.12 L up; the targeteer's at −0.15 L (aft) and −0.04 L, as fractions of the nose-to-tail length; a turret's separation is exactly zero. The same geometry on rotors, on the wing and through a transition, and the same on every 2525 vehicle — read from the controls schema, never retyped.
crs.metric: 28.5 cm between the eyes on the 0.7777 m foil in every mode; turret 0; no second geometry in the source
crs.dtm: a crew's pictures agree the same way through a transition
crs.stretch: a Manta or a droid inherits its parallax from its own length

crs.title: Amber, then red — no shot without a second authority
crs.statement: A designation (button, key, tap, or spoken 'target') puts a door in a slot as AMBER and cannot fire. Only APPROVE — a second person over the link, or the same person acting explicitly as HI-2 — turns it RED, and the record says which of those it was. FIRE, a double-tap and a spoken 'fire' share one path and are refused with NO_RED_BOX or AMBER_NO_APPROVE; every refusal is recorded as a decision, never merely toasted.
crs.metric: approve() is the only writer of red; a double-tap on a fresh mark is a refusal; two-step and two-person told apart
crs.dtm: a first mark can never be a shot
crs.stretch: the second authority arrives over the crew link

crs.title: The decision record and the replay hash
crs.statement: Every designate, approve, refusal, hold and shot is a decision with a sequence id, a named actor, designated, hiApproved, authorityLevel, challenge, diff and the ledger's revision. The feed line is time | actor | verb | id | result. The replay hash is FNV-1a 64 over exactly r.043's projection — no wall-clock, no ISO, no FPS, no SID — and free-form notes sit beside the stream and are never hashed.
crs.metric: a note carrying 'fps 58.3 sid 9f3a' does not move the hash; a different game time does not either; the same round replays to the same hash
crs.dtm: two runs can say WHICH row they disagreed at
crs.stretch: the sidecar beside the immutable Cup fixture

crs.title: The operator deck: keys, sticks, touch and voice
crs.statement: EXEL-2525-CONTROLS-1 is the one map on every 2525 vehicle: L stick BODY (W A S D), R stick HEAD (arrows), Q E turn, U J climb, T next door, 1 2 3 the slots, F fire, C capture. Keys write the refs a thumb does; arrows and the R stick are one gimbal rate inside the declared limits; a tap marks, a double-tap fires only red, the aiming seat's drag looks; voice is offered, never required; calibration is persisted so a resting thumb reads zero; the keymap prints. Typing never flies.
crs.metric: schema held field for field against r.050; arrows do not move the airframe; a 6% resting thumb reads zero; no gesture reaches a shot without canFire
crs.dtm: a person flies and aims with what is in front of them
crs.stretch: the same deck on the turret, the Manta, the Ark and the droid

crs.title: Compare on what he asked to compare on
crs.statement: Every rung of the ladder reports designation rate, HI holds, auth failures, handoffs, simulation speed and a replay hash beside the three it already measured — not winners only. HI holds read zero in the contest and say so, because the contest models a person as a latency and never as a refusal; the holds that are real live in the decision record. Simulation speed is a wall-clock throughput and is never inside the hash.
crs.metric: the same seed replays to the same hash at every rung; level 3 refuses far fewer fire-ticks than level 1
crs.dtm: a rung can be compared with yesterday's
crs.stretch: the Cup fixture replayed against these six

crs.title: CH1–CH5 and DIFF 1–5, from the deck
crs.statement: Five challenges × five difficulties, the deck's challengeSpec verbatim: quota 4+CH×2+DIFF doors in play, window scaled by rate max(10, 56−CH×6−DIFF×4), concurrent doors 1→3, moving from CH3, NET at CH5. Chosen from two dropdowns in the top bar, never a hidden selector. At CH5 NET a red box must come from a second person; self-approval is refused CH5_NO_APPROVE and recorded as a HOLD. TG is not resurrected.
crs.metric: 25 CH×DIFF cells equal to r.050's function; harder is never more time; CH5 self-approval refused and on the record
crs.dtm: a player feels the rung, and CH5 needs two people
crs.stretch: moving targets from the swarm at CH3+

crs.title: The AsM Cup as a regression fixture
crs.statement: ASM_CUP_99.json and ASM_ROSTER.csv are read-only by contract: their bytes are pinned by sha256 and a gate refuses if either moves. The published baseline — seed 2525, 6v6 BLU 3–1, 3v3 BLU 5–0, pairs 1–3 RED and 4–6 BLU at every level — is recomputed from the fixture's numbers, not restated. A new run writes a sidecar beside the fixture, never at it. The fixture's declared revision (0.039) is reported and flagged, not gated.
crs.metric: two hashes pinned; four baseline sentences recomputed; roster = the twelve; sidecar path ≠ fixture path; the module imports no filesystem
crs.dtm: a later build is judged against his published result
crs.stretch: the contest replays the Cup at seed 2525 and compares his six

crs.title: The second person, over the link
crs.statement: The targeteer's amber mark goes out on the gimbal word; the pilot's device shows it with an APPROVE button; the approval crosses the link as its own message, authored by seat, applied once by sequence on the device that holds the mark, in the sender's name — so the box reads two-person. A seat cannot approve its own mark through the link: its echo is dropped and the holder refuses a sender equal to the designator.
crs.metric: approve authored by either seat, needs door + slot; duplicate lands once; own echo dropped; holder refuses self
crs.dtm: two phones make one red box, with two names on it
crs.stretch: the same message on the Manta and the droid

crs.title: The platform identities, from the deck
crs.statement: The eight PLATFORM identities are data lifted from the deck — id, label, kind and flight mode — and a gate compares them to r.050's own units table and dropdown. A platform dropdown sits beside the mode row. D1Q QUAD·HOVER has no wing and refuses the transition by name; D1 VTOL flies both; D1F FOIL takes the wing the moment the transition is legal. Platforms that do not exist on this arena are listed and dated, never hidden; the round never forks a second airframe model per platform.
crs.metric: 8 ids, labels, kinds and 3 flight modes equal to r.050; D1Q wing refused; D1F auto-transitions; one airframe model
crs.dtm: the same platform names on the deck and in the app
crs.stretch: Manta, Ark and the droid on their own arenas

crs.title: The range: per-lane pop-ups at 50–300 m, three modes
crs.statement: At CH0 the turret sits on one of 42 lanes and the ten silhouettes of the 9127 Alt-C sheet (50 F · 100 F ×3 · 150 E ×2 · 200 E ×2 · 250 E · 300 E) stand DOWN until their exposure: one plate per lane at a time, in a seeded per-lane order, for 3 s at 50 m rising 1 s per 50 m to 8 s at 300 m, 1.5 s between exposures. TRAINING·RESET raises a downed target on its next scheduled exposure; TRAINING·DOWN keeps it down until RESET; QUAL·40 runs tables I/II/III of 20/10/10 exposures under clocks that cover them (142/75/75 s), one round per exposure, a lapse is an unfired MISS, a table exposes only what it can score, 23/30/36.
crs.metric: 10 silhouettes; exposures 3..8 s by distance; 42 independent lane orders; one round per exposure; 40/40 attainable
crs.verify: frontend/tests/range-2525.test.mjs · frontend/scripts/drone-deck-qa.mjs (RANGE_POP_SCHEDULE, MODE_RESET_RETURNS, MODE_DOWN_STAYS, MODE_QUAL_TIMED, ONE_ROUND_PER_EXPOSURE, TABLE_III_EXPOSES_ONLY_SCORABLE)
crs.dtm: a first-timer sees a target rise, its caption and its seconds, on a phone
crs.stretch: a canonical range clock shared between two phones (r.132)

crs.title: A hit is scale-true; a target that is down is not a target
crs.statement: A silhouette is hit when the pip sits inside its projected outline (CIRCLE inside the aiming circle, else SILHOUETTE), with an angular floor of 3 mrad (min 3 px) so the standard is the same at every zoom and screen size. A plate that is down, falling, or not the lane's current exposure cannot be hit and is never resurrected; when a target goes down (hit or lapsed) its amber/red box goes with it; a miss keeps red for that exposure only and never re-arms the CH5 second authority.
crs.metric: RANGE_HIT_50 / RANGE_HIT_300 aimed hits; RANGE_MISS_300_OFF20; LAPSE_RELEASES_THE_BOX; no simDirect in any range row
crs.dtm: the pip on the silhouette is the whole rule
crs.stretch: an outline test (dome / shoulders) instead of the bounding rectangle

crs.title: One forward basis; one aim from the eye
crs.statement: The camera vector, the projector, the body motion, the lock cone, every aim and every box read ONE basis (fwdOf/rightOf/yawTo, derived from the projector) and ONE world position (worldOf); every aim is computed from the camera eye to the centre of mass (aimUnitAt). Before r.130 the camera vector and the projector disagreed by 180°: the range pit looked away from its plates and left-stick forward flew the airframe away from what the screen showed.
crs.metric: camera forward lands at screen centre at every yaw/tilt; a fixed point slides left when the stick pans right; the body closes on the point on screen at yaw 90°
crs.dtm: forward is what you see
crs.stretch: the same basis lifted into lib/wire-core for every 2525 surface

crs.title: Render honesty: exceptions recorded, must-hit first, the deck's own QA in CI
crs.statement: A render exception is recorded (state.drawErr), never swallowed; a frame stamps that it ran to its last line and a deferred QA row reads it. What you must hit takes the segment budget before the world on every channel. The deck's boot QA (84 rows) runs in headless Chromium in CI against a checked-in row manifest with set equality and a tight red-list; QA snapshots and restores the record and leaves no designation on the first screen.
crs.metric: DRAW_COMPLETES; QA_LEAVES_NO_TRACE; deck-qa manifest equality; only SYNC_DIRECT red on one device
crs.dtm: a green board that cannot lie about the picture
crs.stretch: a completeness assertion that the must-hit set survived the budget

crs.title: Every operator-deck revision documented, chain-hashed, gated
crs.statement: docs/drone-2525/operator-deck/REVISIONS.md carries one entry per carried revision from r.128 — bytes, sha256, shipping commit, what changed, corrections of earlier claims as NEW lines — chained by sha256(prev|rev|sha|bytes); a gate holds every carried file to its row, README HEAD to the last row, and the chain intact; ONE tests/deck-head.mjs names HEAD for every deck-reading gate; the patchers that built each revision are carried beside it.
crs.metric: 4 entries r.128..r.131; chain intact; HEAD constant equal across gates and the PLAY button
crs.dtm: a reviewer can check every revision by hash tomorrow
crs.stretch: a chain that also covers the narrative and the shipping commit, anchored in git

motLadder.note: Band = edge-compute class (how many sensor modules and how much CNN). Step = resolution (pixel density and curve roundness). Rung 1.1 is the 1983 vector arcade and asks for the fastest picture; 5.5 is the dense fused mesh. A higher rung asks for MORE work and therefore FEWER frames per second — demand, not capability.

hal.auto: the unit picks its class from its own measured frame rate
hal.rule: the CNN reserve is subtracted from the frame before the renderer may want any of it

stream.rule: shed a sensor module first, then resolution, then frame rate — and name every step

selfCal.goal: report the highest rung this machine holds at the reference stream

si.ladder: lib/pod-clock.ts — noted 1, adopted 3, foundational 7; nothing in between and nothing above
si.authority: the group advises, a named person decides; nothing in the consensus engine can fire a shot

crew.rule: a seat may only send what that seat controls; the other seat's controls are absent, not disabled
crew.proof: scripts/drone-crew-e2e.mjs — two separate browser profiles, only the cloud path available

swarm.rule: the swarm takes its share of the rung's budget first; every aircraft is drawn before any gets detail
swarm.passMark: 42 aircraft at rung 2.3 holding the 30 Hz reference on a processor slowed ten times

authority.2: a named person, each aircraft once
authority.3: a named person, a declared window
authority.5: the key group's live lean, a standing mandate it can end
authority.invariant: a named human decision exists before any machine shot; silence is never consent at any level
